title: Psoriasis Biologic Classes
subtitle: TNF-α inhibitors vs IL-17 inhibitors vs IL-23 inhibitors

values.tnf: Adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab, certolizumab pegol, golimumab

values.il17: ~12 weeks; bimekizumab notable clearance at 4 weeks

values.tnf: PsA ★ (all 5 agents); IBD (adalimumab, infliximab, certolizumab) ★; ankylosing spondylitis. PREFERRED when IBD comorbidity. Certolizumab PREFERRED in pregnancy.
values.il17: PsA ★ (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab, brodalumab); ankylosing spondylitis. AVOID in IBD (can exacerbate or trigger IBD flares). Preferred for rapid skin clearance.
values.il23: PsA (guselkumab, risankizumab); IBD (risankizumab approved for Crohn's, mirikizumab for UC) ★. Preferred for moderate-severe plaque psoriasis WITHOUT a specific comorbidity preference. Safest class overall.

features.name: Black box warnings and key safety signals

values.tnf: BLACK BOX: serious infections (TB reactivation ★, opportunistic infections), malignancy (lymphoma ★, NMSC). HBV reactivation. Demyelination risk — CONTRAINDICATED in MS. Heart failure exacerbation (avoid in NYHA III–IV). Lupus-like reaction.
values.il17: No black box for most; BRODALUMAB BLACK BOX: suicidal ideation / behavior (REMS program). Class effect: mucocutaneous candidiasis (10–20%; usually mild, responds to fluconazole). IBD exacerbation — do NOT use in active IBD. Neutropenia (monitor CBC).
values.il23: No black box warnings. No REMS. Cleanest safety profile of any biologic class. Rare: upper respiratory infections, injection-site reactions. No signal for IBD exacerbation. No increased malignancy signal to date.

values.tnf: Adalimumab: SC q2w. Etanercept: SC q1–2w. Infliximab: IV infusion (0, 2, 6 wk → q8w). Certolizumab: SC q2w. Golimumab: SC q4w or IV.
values.il17: Secukinumab: SC q4w after loading. Ixekizumab: SC q2w × 12 wk then q4w. Bimekizumab: SC q4w × 16 wk then q8w. Brodalumab: SC q2w after loading.
values.il23: Guselkumab: SC at 0, 4 wk → q8w. Risankizumab: SC at 0, 4 wk → q12w. Tildrakizumab: SC at 0, 4 wk → q12w. Mirikizumab: SC at 0, 4, 8 wk → q8w.

values.tnf: HIGHEST risk: TNF-α is critical for granuloma maintenance. Screen with QuantiFERON-TB Gold before starting. LTBI treatment required before initiation (9 months INH or 4 months rifampin). Annual surveillance if ongoing high-risk exposure.
values.il17: Lower risk than TNF inhibitors; IL-17 less critical for TB granuloma. Screen at baseline (QuantiFERON-TB Gold) per guidelines. Some guidelines allow biologic initiation after ≥1 month of LTBI treatment.
values.il23: Lowest class risk; IL-23 less critical for granuloma integrity than TNF. Screen at baseline. Some evidence that LTBI treatment can be initiated concurrently (not proven as safe as with TNF — consult ID).

values.tnf: Certolizumab pegol PREFERRED — Fc-free, minimal placental transfer (<1%); can be continued throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding. Adalimumab/etanercept: low transfer in 1st–2nd trimester; consider stopping in 3rd trimester. Neonates exposed to IgG-Fc TNF inhibitors in 3rd trimester: no live vaccines for 6 months.
values.il17: INSUFFICIENT safety data for pregnancy. Animal studies show some risk at high doses. Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Switch to certolizumab or NB-UVB before conception.
values.il23: INSUFFICIENT safety data for pregnancy. Not recommended. NB-UVB and certolizumab are preferred alternatives during pregnancy.

features.name: Time to assess response and monitoring

values.tnf: Assess at 12 weeks. Therapeutic drug level monitoring available for adalimumab and infliximab (detect antidrug antibodies). Annual screen: CBC, LFTs. Infliximab: pre-infusion checks each visit.
values.il17: Assess at 12 weeks (IL-17A) or 16 weeks (bimekizumab). Routine labs not required; CBC if neutropenia concern. Monitor for candidiasis and IBD symptoms.
values.il23: Assess at 16 weeks (longer induction response curve). No routine lab monitoring required. Reassess at 16 and 28 weeks before considering switch. Durable response minimizes need for frequent monitoring.
